mbm-1276.clue: I keep a spare sunrise rolled up.
mbm-1276.quote: I painted the dawn backdrop for a school play. It hangs behind the sofa between shows. On winter mornings my brother unrolls a corner and says the sun has at least made an effort.

mbm-1277.clue: I stitched a bowl of stars.
mbm-1277.quote: My quilt shows my aunt’s blue mixing bowl with little stars rising from it instead of steam. She taught me to bake and to sew. I couldn’t decide which lesson to draw first.

mbm-1278.clue: I got the tune on the third cup of tea.
mbm-1278.quote: At our traditional music session I listened through the first two rounds with my fiddle on my knee. I found the B part just as someone set down my tea. By the time I drank it, it was cold and the tune was mine.

mbm-1279.clue: I’m learning the weather by ear.
mbm-1279.quote: I tune the radio just before dawn and swap weather notes with a gardener across the water. When I heard rain tapping her greenhouse roof, I moved my washing indoors. Her forecast arrived a full cup of tea early.

mbm-1280.clue: I stitched the train from memory.
mbm-1280.quote: I made a quilt for my brother with the local train running along one edge. Mum spotted the little cream carriage where she used to pass us orange slices. I’d forgotten the oranges, but I’d remembered the window.

mbm-1281.clue: I brought a bib for the judge.
mbm-1281.quote: There was a blueberry eating contest at our picnic and my first berry bounced clean off the plate onto the judge’s notebook. Next year I gave him a little purple bib before I sat down.

mbm-1282.clue: I’m looking for the owner of a recipe.
mbm-1282.quote: Tucked inside an old novel I found a recipe for lemon buns in blue ink. I baked a batch and took them to my reading group. Nobody recognized the handwriting, but six people asked for the recipe.

mbm-1283.clue: I put an ear on the jam pot.
mbm-1283.quote: My ceramic jar came out shaped like a sleepy rabbit if you looked sideways. I added a second ear to the lid and painted the nose pink. At breakfast we lift the rabbit by its ears and find plum jam.

mbm-1284.clue: I made room for the shadow.
mbm-1284.quote: In late-afternoon beach volleyball the net stretches a long shadow across the court. My friend took a photograph of us jumping over that shadow. Our feet look miles off the ground.

mbm-1285.clue: I keep the spoon in the landscape.
mbm-1285.quote: I used the back of a silver teaspoon as a mirror and painted the mountains I saw in it. The hills came out bent around the little bowl. My sister asked for a whole place setting of mountain views.

mbm-1286.clue: My tape measure wanted to draw the snail.
mbm-1286.quote: I let go of my tape measure and it curled up on the cloth. I traced the spiral for a snail's shell on Dad's quilt. He follows it with his finger and announces how many inches the snail hasn't traveled.

mbm-1287.clue: I buy the front-row seat nobody wants.
mbm-1287.quote: In our tiny cinema the first row has a chipped wall tile beside the screen. Before every show a little reflected flicker runs across it. I’ve started to think of that flicker as the opening act.

mbm-1288.clue: I thought the post was wearing a hat.
mbm-1288.quote: I watched a little brown owl settle on the fence post at dusk. It sat so still that my neighbor hung his coat on the next post before he noticed. The owl opened one eye and went on being a hat.

mbm-1289.clue: I keep one map folded the wrong way.
mbm-1289.quote: The crease hides the big monuments and opens to a little square where a man sells striped balloons. On my sightseeing day I sat there long enough to draw every color.

mbm-1290.clue: I designed the world’s laziest ramp.
mbm-1290.quote: I made a mini-golf obstacle with a groove so shallow the ball takes ages to come back out. We time the trip with my cousin singing. His longest song is the official course record.

mbm-1291.clue: I picked the loudest room in a quiet museum.
mbm-1291.quote: At the instrument museum a guide let me turn the crank on a little street organ. Three strangers stopped and tapped their shoes together. My hands were shaking, but the tune kept going.

mbm-1292.clue: I always read the restorer’s card.
mbm-1292.quote: A museum painting had a photograph beside it showing the canvas half cleaned. I stood on tiptoe looking for the line between the two halves. My own reflection in the glass kept passing from dusk into daylight.

mbm-1293.clue: I have a hat from a tournament I lost.
mbm-1293.quote: I played in a windy charity round and my cap sailed into the pond. The groundskeeper gave me a faded bucket hat. My whole group signed the brim after we finally finished.

mbm-1294.clue: I pace myself by the accordion.
mbm-1294.quote: Our eating contest shares a tent with a little band. I put my fork down whenever the accordion takes a solo. I always hear the best music and still manage a respectable number of dumplings.

mbm-1295.clue: I cut my first leather rose at midnight.
mbm-1295.quote: I was repairing a bag and the red offcut curled into a petal. I kept cutting until I had a whole rose for the clasp. The repair took all evening. The flower was worth staying up for.

mbm-1296.clue: I took a very small victory lap.
mbm-1296.quote: My neighbour won the pie contest and I came last, but I got the final slice of apricot. I carried my plate once around our picnic table. Nobody argued with my definition of victory.

mbm-1297.clue: I wrote a waltz for a clothes peg.
mbm-1297.quote: I clipped a wooden peg to the paper holding my cuatro tune. In the breeze it tapped the stand in three beats. I played along and named the tune after the cheapest percussionist I’ve ever hired.

mbm-1298.clue: I lace the shoes in two colors.
mbm-1298.quote: One red lace and one blue keep my bowling shoes apart from my brother’s identical pair. He wore them to throw a strike last month. Now he’s claiming custody of the lucky laces.

mbm-1299.clue: I bring a little desk bell to the roof.
mbm-1299.quote: On sunny days we lounge on separate rooftops across a narrow alley. My neighbor rings a bell when her lemonade is ready, and I ring mine when I’ve found the deck of cards.

mbm-1300.quote: On pajama movie nights I put two kernels into each folded paper invitation. My sister brings hers back to pop with the rest. We call the very last pop our missing guest.
